THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by appellant/accused No.4 in crime No.137/2022 of Nanjanagudu Town Police Station, Mysore registered for the offences punishable under Sections 403, 406, 420 and 114 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as the "IPC" for short) and under Section 9 of The Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments Act, 2004 (KPIDFE Act, for short).

entities.text: Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments Act, 2004
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The Court of Prl.District and Sessions Judge at Mysuru vide order dated 03.03.2023 passed in Crl.Misc.No.129/2023 has rejected the application filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. which has resulted in filing this appeal under Section 16 of the KPIDFE Act.

entities.text: Prl.District and Sessions Judge at Mysuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and learned High Court Government Pleader for the State and perused the material available on record.

4. In the complaint lodged by S.Shivaswamy, he has alleged that one Shambulingu M., working as a teacher, induced him to open an account in a chit fund run by him in the name of his wife Smt.B.Dakshayini (Accused No.1) and upon his insistence, the complainant joined two chits of Rs.5,00,000/- each, which commenced on 15.11.2017 and 10.01.2018 respectively and he used to pay Rs.20,000/- every month through cash and in all he has paid the entire chit amount of Rs.10,00,000/-.
The said two chits came to be matured on 15.11.2020 and 10.01.2022.
Whenever he demanded for the chit amount, they postponed the same on one or the other pretext.
After few months, the accused made a part payment of Rs.15,000/- on July 2022 to him.
But, later he came to known that the said Shambulingu committed suicide.
When he went and requested accused no.1 to return the NC: 2024:KHC:10237 chit amount, the said accused without repaying the amount vacated the house and fled away etc.

2 5.

sentences.text:
It is alleged that accused No.1 and her husband collected huge amount from many depositors and cheated them and from the proceeds, they purchased properties in the name of accused Nos.2 to 4.
6.

The learned High Court Government Pleader contended that accused Nos.1 to 4 have colluded with each other and persuaded the public to join the chit and received deposits from various persons and after collecting huge amount, cheated them.
He contends that in the present case the complainant has been cheated to the tune of Rs.10,00,000/-.

He further contended that the petition preferred under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. is not maintainable, since the accused have committed an offence under the KPIDFE Act and as per Section 18 (2) of the said act, the learned Sessions Judge has rightly rejected the prayer seeking anticipatory bail.

The learned Sessions Judge has relied on a decision of this Court in Shreesha Sasithota Prabhakaran Vs. The State of Karnataka in (Crl.P.No.9971/2022) dated 10.11.2022 and rejected the prayer seeking anticipatory bail, observing that the provisions of Section 438 of Cr.P.C. are not applicable, since the KPIDFE Act has overriding effect, over all other provisions of Law.

entities.text: Shreesha Sasithota Prabhakaran Vs. The State of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is observed that in this case, Section 9 of the KPIDFE Act, 2004 is invoked and therefore, the accused is not entitled for the grant of anticipatory bail, as the very petition is not maintainable in view of the clear bar under Section 18 (2) of the said Act.

8. One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that Section 9 of the KPIDFE Act is not applicable to the case on hand, since the definition of "deposit" does not include the amount received by way of subscription, in respect of a chit.

It is therefore contended by the learned counsel that the decision referred to by the learned Sessions Judge is not NC:
2024:KHC:10237 applicable and the learned Sessions Judge was not right in rejecting the petition seeking anticipatory bail holding that the same is not maintainable in view of Section 18(2) of the KPIDFE Act.
9.
As per the definition of "deposit" provided under Section 2(2) (vii) of KPIDFE Act, "deposit" does not include the amount received by way of subscription in respect of a chit.

In the present case, the offence alleged under the KPIDFE Act is one under Section 9 of the said Act, i.e., any financial establishment fraudulently committing default in the repayment of 'deposit' etc.
Hence, it cannot be said that a prima facie case is made out against the appellant, at this stage, which would attract the provisions of the said act.

10. The allegations are that the accused have colluded with other and collected huge amount from the complainant and similar other persons by inducing them to join the chit and later invested the amount in properties in the names of accused Nos.2 to 4 and cheated the NC: 2024:KHC:10237 complainant and other depositors without returning their amount.

11. A perusal of the complaint averments would reveal that one Shambulingu, working as a teacher,
met the complainant and he insisted him to join the chit which was being run in the name of his wife i.e., accused No.1.
The said Shambulingu committed suicide on 03.11.2022.

On coming to know Shri M S.Sathish vs State Of Karnataka on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42260337/
3 about him committing suicide, when the complainant requested accused No.1 to return the matured amount, initially he was promised that the amount would be returned, but later it is alleged that the said accused vacated the house and all the accused in collusion with each others cheated the complainant and similar other depositors.
12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The prosecution has to establish it's case in due course.
The offences alleged are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
During the pendency of this appeal, interim bail was granted to the appellant on 21.04.2023.

It is submitted that the appellant has NC: 2024:KHC:10237 appeared before the Investigating Officer and executed the bond with a surety as specified in the order and co- operated with the investigation.
13.
In the above facts and circumstances, the relief sought in this appeal can be granted by imposing necessary conditions.

Accordingly the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed.
ii) The order dated 03.03.2023 passed in Crl.Misc.129/2023 by the Court of Prl.District and Sessions Judge at Mysuru is set aside.

entities.text: Court of Prl.District and Sessions Judge at Mysuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
iii) The order dated 21.04.2023, granting interim bail to the appellant/accused No.4 is made absolute with further conditions as under:
a.
The appellant/accused No.4 shall be available for the purpose of investigation as and when required and he shall co- operate with the investigation.
He shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses/evidence in any manner.
c. He shall furnish proof of his residential address and shall inform the Investigating Officer/Court, if there is any change in the address.
d. He shall be regular in attending the Court proceedings.
